    // The smallest of an array of distances.
    NearestDistance(distances: Array<Number>): Number
        => distances.Reduce(Number.MaxValue, (acc, d) => acc.Min(d));

    // The smallest distance strictly greater than `nearest` — the second feature
    // distance, given the first. Ties with `nearest` are skipped, so a point
    // equidistant from two features reports the next distinct feature.
    SecondNearestDistance(distances: Array<Number>, nearest: Number): Number
        => distances.Reduce(Number.MaxValue, (acc, d) => d <= nearest ? acc : acc.Min(d));

    //==
    // # Basis dispatch
    //
    // The fractal and warped noises are parameterized by a `NoiseBasis` case, not
    // by a basis field value, so they need one entry point turning a case plus
    // (seed, frequency) into a sample. Worley and Gabor carry parameters the
    // enumeration cannot express; neutral choices stand in, and a field wanting
    // others uses that basis type directly rather than through a fractal.
    // Every case is remapped to the same nominal [-1, 1] so octaves of different
    // bases sum sensibly; the White and Worley shifts are not exact at the ends.

    // A sample of the named basis noise at the given seed and frequency.
    BasisValue2D(basis: NoiseBasis, seed: Integer, frequency: Number, p: Point2D): Number
        => match (basis) {
            White => WhiteNoise2D(seed).Eval(p) * 2.0 - 1.0;
            Value => ValueNoise2D(seed, frequency).Eval(p);
            Perlin => PerlinNoise2D(seed, frequency).Eval(p);
            Simplex => SimplexNoise2D(seed, frequency).Eval(p);
            Worley => 1.0 - 2.0 * WorleyNoise2D(seed, frequency, 1.0,
                                                WorleyDistance.Euclidean, WorleyFeature.F1).Eval(p);
            Gabor => GaborNoise2D(seed, frequency, 0.0.Turns, 1.0, 0.0).Eval(p);
        };

    // A sample of the named basis noise at the given seed and frequency.
    BasisValue3D(basis: NoiseBasis, seed: Integer, frequency: Number, p: Point3D): Number
        => match (basis) {
            White => WhiteNoise3D(seed).Eval(p) * 2.0 - 1.0;
            Value => ValueNoise3D(seed, frequency).Eval(p);
            Perlin => PerlinNoise3D(seed, frequency).Eval(p);
            Simplex => SimplexNoise3D(seed, frequency).Eval(p);
            Worley => 1.0 - 2.0 * WorleyNoise3D(seed, frequency, 1.0,
                                                WorleyDistance.Euclidean, WorleyFeature.F1).Eval(p);
            Gabor => GaborNoise3D(seed, frequency, Direction3D(Vector3D.UnitZ), 1.0, 0.0).Eval(p);
        };

    //==
    // # Basis noise evaluation
    //
    // The `Eval` bodies for the single-octave noise fields of
    // `noise.types.plato`, written against the shared lattice vocabulary above
    // (hashing, gradients, feature points, metrics). The
    // fractal sums below layer these.
    //
    // Every body multiplies the query point by Frequency first, so a lattice cell is
    // one unit wide in the working coordinates and `Floor` gives the cell index.
    // Scalar output ranges over [-1, 1] except white noise, which is [0, 1) as its
    // declaration says.
    //
    // The gradient noises interpolate with `SmootherStep` (Perlin's quintic fade),
    // not `SmoothStep`: the cubic leaves a second-derivative discontinuity at the
    // lattice planes that shows up as banding once the field is differentiated, which
    // the fractal and warped noises do constantly.

    //==
    // # White noise
    //
    // No lattice and no interpolation: the coordinates themselves are hashed, so
    // two points however close have unrelated values.

    // The uncorrelated value at this point, in [0, 1).
    Eval(self: WhiteNoise2D, p: Point2D): Number
        => HashToUnit(LatticeHash(self.Seed, p.X.Hash, p.Y.Hash));

    // The uncorrelated value at this point, in [0, 1).
    Eval(self: WhiteNoise3D, p: Point3D): Number
        => HashToUnit(LatticeHash(self.Seed, p.X.Hash, p.Y.Hash, p.Z.Hash));

    //==
    // # Value noise
    //
    // One random value per lattice corner, faded between them. Cheap, and the
    // extrema sit ON the lattice, which is the lattice artifact the type's doc
    // comment warns about.

    // The faded bilinear blend of the four surrounding corner values.
    Eval(self: ValueNoise2D, p: Point2D): Number {
        var x = p.X * self.Frequency;
        var y = p.Y * self.Frequency;
        var i = x.Floor.ToInteger;
        var j = y.Floor.ToInteger;
        var u = (x - x.Floor).SmootherStep;
        var v = (y - y.Floor).SmootherStep;
        var c00 = HashToSigned(LatticeHash(self.Seed, i, j));
        var c10 = HashToSigned(LatticeHash(self.Seed, i + 1, j));
        var c01 = HashToSigned(LatticeHash(self.Seed, i, j + 1));
        var c11 = HashToSigned(LatticeHash(self.Seed, i + 1, j + 1));
        return c00.Lerp(c10, u).Lerp(c01.Lerp(c11, u), v);
    }

    // The faded trilinear blend of the eight surrounding corner values.
    Eval(self: ValueNoise3D, p: Point3D): Number {
        var x = p.X * self.Frequency;
        var y = p.Y * self.Frequency;
        var z = p.Z * self.Frequency;
        var i = x.Floor.ToInteger;
        var j = y.Floor.ToInteger;
        var k = z.Floor.ToInteger;
        var u = (x - x.Floor).SmootherStep;
        var v = (y - y.Floor).SmootherStep;
        var w = (z - z.Floor).SmootherStep;
        var c000 = HashToSigned(LatticeHash(self.Seed, i, j, k));
        var c100 = HashToSigned(LatticeHash(self.Seed, i + 1, j, k));
        var c010 = HashToSigned(LatticeHash(self.Seed, i, j + 1, k));
        var c110 = HashToSigned(LatticeHash(self.Seed, i + 1, j + 1, k));
        var c001 = HashToSigned(LatticeHash(self.Seed, i, j, k + 1));
        var c101 = HashToSigned(LatticeHash(self.Seed, i + 1, j, k + 1));
        var c011 = HashToSigned(LatticeHash(self.Seed, i, j + 1, k + 1));
        var c111 = HashToSigned(LatticeHash(self.Seed, i + 1, j + 1, k + 1));
        var lo = c000.Lerp(c100, u).Lerp(c010.Lerp(c110, u), v);
        var hi = c001.Lerp(c101, u).Lerp(c011.Lerp(c111, u), v);
        return lo.Lerp(hi, w);
    }

    //==
    // # Perlin gradient noise
    //
    // One random unit GRADIENT per lattice corner; each corner contributes the
    // dot product of its gradient with the offset to the query point, so the
    // field is zero at every corner. The trailing constants normalize the
    // theoretical extremum (sqrt(N)/2 for unit gradients in N dimensions) back to
    // one. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perlin_noise

    // The faded blend of the four corner gradient contributions.
    Eval(self: PerlinNoise2D, p: Point2D): Number {
        var x = p.X * self.Frequency;
        var y = p.Y * self.Frequency;
        var i = x.Floor.ToInteger;
        var j = y.Floor.ToInteger;
        var dx = x - x.Floor;
        var dy = y - y.Floor;
        var u = dx.SmootherStep;
        var v = dy.SmootherStep;
        var n00 = LatticeGradient2D(self.Seed, i, j).Dot((dx, dy));
        var n10 = LatticeGradient2D(self.Seed, i + 1, j).Dot((dx - 1.0, dy));
        var n01 = LatticeGradient2D(self.Seed, i, j + 1).Dot((dx, dy - 1.0));
        var n11 = LatticeGradient2D(self.Seed, i + 1, j + 1).Dot((dx - 1.0, dy - 1.0));
        return n00.Lerp(n10, u).Lerp(n01.Lerp(n11, u), v) * Number.SqrtTwo;
    }
